ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion — explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you actually bet?
Most bettors guess. Kelly has an answer.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat betting without thinking about edge.

If you bet the same amount on a 52% edge and a 58% edge, you're leaving money on the table — or risking too much on thin spots.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
The Kelly criterion sizes your bet based on two things:
your estimated edge and the odds on offer.

Bigger edge + better odds = larger bet. Thin edge = smaller bet. No edge = no bet.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Simple example:
You estimate 56% win probability. Odds are -110 (implied 52.4%).

Full Kelly says bet about 6.5% of your bankroll.
Most sharp bettors use half-Kelly (3.25%) to smooth out variance.
Still far more than gut-feel sizing.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need a formula tattooed on your wrist.
You need the concept: bet more when your edge is real, less when it's thin.

Save this. It's the most useful risk framework in betting.
